title: 4D Transvaginal Ultrasonography as a First-Line Non-Invasive Follow-Up After Hysteroscopic Metroplasty in Dysmorphic Uterus Cases
content:
Aim: This study compared the cost-effectiveness of 4D-transvaginal ultrasonography (TVUSG), hysterosalpingography (HSG), and hysteroscopy (HS) in evaluating postoperative uterine correction in patients who underwent hysteroscopic metroplasty for a dysmorphic uterus. Additionally, pregnancy outcomes following surgery were assessed.

Materials and Methods: Thirty-one patients who underwent hysteroscopic metroplasty due to a dysmorphic uterus between July 2023 and June 2024 were retrospectively analysed. Postoperative uterine cavity evaluations were performed using 4D-TVUSG. Alternative imaging modalities (HSG and HS) were compared in terms of invasiveness, feasibility and cost based on official ministry of health data. One-year postoperative pregnancy outcomes were also recorded.

Results: 4D-TVUSG was found to be superior to HSG and HS due to its non-invasive nature, ease of use, no need for anaesthesia, and lower cost. Postoperatively, 14 patients (45.2%) achieved pregnancy, of whom 3 (21.4%) experienced miscarriages and 11 (78.6%) had ongoing pregnancies or live births. All patients demonstrated a normalised uterine cavity on follow-up and a 100% surgical success rate.

Conclusion: 4D-TVUSG is a reliable, cost-effective, and non-invasive method for postoperative assessment in patients with a dysmorphic uterus undergoing hysteroscopic metroplasty. This is the first study to compare the cost-effectiveness of these three imaging methods, highlighting 4D-TVUSG as a potential first-line follow-up tool in clinical practice.
